text: Welcome to the updated Iron Meridian student walkthrough. This AI-narrated recording uses the real website and disposable demonstration data, not verified classroom evidence. I enter my first and last name, learner email, instructor email, and team number once. Our team uses one saved submission and shares its private resume link only with teammates. Choice questions check automatically. Every typed or written response needs instructor acceptance before it earns points. I keep my private resume token so we can continue our saved work.

Welcome to the updated Silent Lantern student walkthrough. This AI-narrated recording uses isolated demonstration data, not a live UFED extraction or verified classroom findings. I enter my first and last name, learner email, instructor email, and team number, and acknowledge the classroom rules. Our team uses one saved submission and keeps its resume link private. Choice questions check automatically. Every non-choice answer, including typed flags, needs instructor acceptance. A denied answer must be meaningfully revised and accepted before we can continue.

The final section moves from analysis to dissemination and the commander's brief. I answer the choice questions, then submit the required written products for acceptance. A useful brief separates confirmed findings, analytical judgments, and remaining gaps, and cites its supporting evidence. The responses shown here are illustrative examples, not verified classroom findings. I check the instructor's feedback and wait for each non-choice response to be accepted. Those accepted responses now earn their full question points automatically. Saving an answer alone does not award those points or complete the exercise.

I open Results and check that every question is correct or accepted. Accepted non-choice responses have their full points included automatically. I submit the final results and confirm the submitted state. The Leaderboard tab shows only our team number, a progress bar, and percentage; there are no student names, emails, answers, or scores. One hundred percent means every choice is correct and every non-choice answer is accepted. The instructor receives an in-site completion notification. Email delivery is separate and requires a configured mail service.

This updated Iron Meridian instructor walkthrough explains the shared-team review process. The recording and AI narration use isolated demonstration records, not real students or verified evidence. Before class, prepare the assigned extraction and explain that each team uses one saved submission. Students enter their identity, both email addresses, and team number once, then resume using the team's private link. Keep your instructor code private. I open Instructor and unlock the console using a disposable test code.

This updated Silent Lantern instructor walkthrough uses isolated demonstration data and AI narration. Brief the class on the six UFED-only missions, assigned evidence, and classroom rules. Each team uses one saved submission and keeps its private resume link within the team. Students enter their details and team number once. Explain that every non-choice response, including typed flags, now requires acceptance; denial requires a meaningful revision. I unlock Instructor with a disposable test code, not a classroom credential.

Use the answer guide to prepare all eight sections and distinguish active choice keys, evidence references, and illustrative written examples. Verify dataset-dependent choice keys against the actual classroom extraction before saving them. Do not copy these demonstration values. All non-choice questions now go to instructor acceptance even when a reference answer exists. Ask students to show the source artifact, explain their method, and state a limitation. Use the guide to assess that reasoning rather than treating the sample wording as the only acceptable response.

Prepare each mission with the answer guide and the assigned UFED evidence. Existing dataset references help you review the same-iPhone Major match, courier alias, and final watchlist keyword; typed flags still require instructor acceptance. Review each team's own SIM IMSI individually, including supported no-content findings. Do not replace a team's SIM evidence with another team's value. Keep the activity UFED-only and treat Preserved Extraction and SafeGuard as knowledge topics. Ask learners to show their source and explain their reasoning, not merely repeat a sample answer.

Choose Open review queue to see every latest nonblank non-choice response awaiting a decision. You do not have to open students one at a time. Each entry identifies the team, learner name, question, response, and submission time. Sort oldest or newest first, or by names in either direction. The queue refreshes every five seconds. Schedule frequent review check-ins so teams are not left waiting. Read the actual response and compare it with the team's evidence before choosing one of the three review actions.

This response is too vague to support acceptance. The feedback actions are disabled until I enter a note. I explain what needs to change, then choose Deny with feedback. The denied response earns zero points and leaves the pending queue until the team revises it. The learner sees the feedback and must meaningfully revise and resubmit; an unchanged answer cannot be accepted. Confirm the saved decision rather than assuming a button click succeeded. A failed request must not be mistaken for a saved review.

The team has submitted a revised response, which returns to pending review. I read the current wording before deciding. If a revision arrives while I am reviewing, the controls ask me to acknowledge that I have read it; a stale decision cannot accept a newer response. I add useful feedback and choose Accept with feedback. The full question points are added automatically and the item leaves the queue. In Silent Lantern, acceptance also clears that response's progression gate; all other requirements must still be met.

For a response that meets the criteria without needing a note, choose Accept response. No feedback is required for this action. It awards the full question points automatically, just like Accept with feedback. I do not type or calculate the points manually. A learner's later edit removes the acceptance and those points until the changed response is reviewed again. Review the current evidence consistently across teams.

The Completions area gives instructors an in-site notification when a team reaches full completion. These notifications persist, so returning later still shows unread completions. Mark them read after checking the result; polling does not create duplicate notifications for the same completion. The separate Leaderboard tab shows only team labels, progress bars, and percentages. Progress counts correct choices and accepted non-choice responses, not simply answered questions or bonus points. A team reaches one hundred percent only when every question meets its completion rule.

Finish by checking the pending queue, having teams submit their final results, and debriefing their evidence and limitations. In-site completion alerts are not email receipts; mail delivery needs its own configured service. Keep student information and answer guides off a shared projector, and lock the instructor console when finished. This demonstration did not send real emails or alter classroom records.

This short Iron Meridian guide shows the updated process for completing the CTF as a team. It uses the actual website, AI narration, and isolated demonstration data. First, one team representative enters the required names, email addresses, and team number. Teammates reuse the same saved submission through its private resume link. Do not create a second submission for the same team or share the private link outside the team.

This short Silent Lantern guide shows the updated process for completing the six-mission CTF. It uses the real website, AI narration, and illustrative demonstration data. One representative registers the team and acknowledges the classroom rules. Teammates continue the same saved submission through its private resume link. Use only the assigned UFED evidence and stay within the training scope; this recording is not a hardware extraction.

Work through the choice questions using your assigned evidence. Save and validate the selected answer. If it is incorrect, use the coaching to decide what to inspect again; it does not reveal the correct option. Correct choices add points automatically. A multiple-selection question requires the requested complete set without extra choices. Saved progress lets your team continue later without entering identity details again.

For any typed or written response, enter your answer and submit it for instructor acceptance. A saved draft is not an accepted answer and earns no points while pending. Read the instructor's feedback. If denied, meaningfully revise and resubmit the response; repeating the same wording does not satisfy the requirement. When accepted, its full question points are added automatically. In Silent Lantern, you must clear the current approval gate before moving forward.

The instructor opens the review queue, sorts by submission time or name, and checks the current response against the evidence. Accept response needs no note. Accept with feedback and Deny with feedback require a note. Every acceptance awards the full question points. Revisions return to pending and require another decision. This keeps the learner's score and progress tied to the latest reviewed work, not an older answer.

When every choice is correct and every non-choice response is accepted, open Results and review the saved answers, feedback, and total points. Submit the final results and confirm that the site records the submission. An answered count alone is not completion. If you edit an accepted answer afterward, its acceptance and points are removed until the instructor reviews the revision.

Use the Leaderboard tab to view each team's progress bar and percentage. It shows team numbers only, not student names, emails, answers, or scores. One hundred percent means all questions are correct or accepted. The instructor receives a persistent in-site completion notification and can mark it read. This is separate from email delivery, which requires a configured mail service. Keep your team's resume link private and finish with an evidence-focused debrief.
